paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD has done wonders, so the psalm says to sing Him a NEW song (Psalm 98:1). His right hand and holy arm gained Him the victory, and nobody else had to carry it for Him. He also remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel, and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God (Psalm 98:3).

So the song isn't about how good the singer is, and that is GREAT news for me. The psalm asks for a joyful noise, not a perfect one (Psalm 98:4). It calls on all the earth, and it even invites the sea and all that fills it (Psalm 98:7). If the rivers get to clap, friend, you can open your mouth too.

Then comes the part that might sound scary. The psalm says the LORD comes to judge the earth, and still it calls creation to sing for joy before Him (Psalm 98:9). That's because He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity. So when you sing today, sing LOUD, and let the reason be who He is and what He has done.
